title: Quebec’s Coalition Avenir Québec won 13% of the votes and no seats; a party with 12% won 9
body: On 5 October 2026 Quebec elected its 127-seat National Assembly by first past the post: each riding is a separate race, and the candidate with the most votes wins its seat, even without a majority. According to [Élections Québec](https://www.electionsquebec.qc.ca/resultats-et-statistiques/resultats-generales/2026-10-05/), the Coalition Avenir Québec (CAQ), which had won 90 of 125 seats in 2022, got 13.35% of the votes and no seats: its support was spread thinly across the province, and it came second in 19 ridings but first in none. Québec solidaire got fewer votes, 12.42%, but they were packed into city ridings such as Gouin, where it won 62.61%, so it took 9 seats. The Parti Québécois won 60 seats, 47% of them, with 28.02% of the votes; in 42 of its wins it had less than 40%. Across the province, the winner had under half of the votes in 100 of the 127 ridings. The same thing happened to the Conservative Party of Quebec in 2022: 12.91% of the votes and no seats.

slides.question: In Quebec’s 5 October 2026 election, the Parti Québécois won 28% of the votes. What share of the 127 seats did it win?
slides.explanation: 60 of 127 seats, about 47%. It came first in 60 ridings (electoral districts), 42 of them with less than 40% of the votes, and first place is all it takes.

slides.alt: Animation on cream paper: Quebec's 127 ridings as coloured tiles, then cards for Coalition Avenir Québec, 13.35% and 0 seats, and Québec solidaire, 12.42% and 9. A riding won with 26.03%, strip charts of each party's share in every riding, bars of votes against seats, and dots spread or packed.

slides.prompt: Spread your party’s 13% of the votes over fewer or more of ten ridings. Find a spread that wins three seats.
slides.takeaway: Packed into three ridings, 13% of the votes wins 3 of 10 seats. Spread over four or more it wins none, and packed into two it piles up votes it doesn’t need. Same votes, different places.

slides.heading: Votes for each seat won, Quebec, 5 October 2026
slides.note: Coalition Avenir Québec’s 572,040 votes won no seat. Élections Québec, final results.

left.label: 2022, 125 seats
left.text: Coalition Avenir Québec: 40.98% of the votes and 90 seats. Conservative Party of Quebec: 12.91% and no seats.

right.label: 2026, 127 seats
right.text: Coalition Avenir Québec: 13.35% of the votes and no seats. Conservative Party of Quebec: 20.66% and 19 seats.

slides.question: Under first past the post, what does a candidate need to win a riding’s seat?
options: More votes than anyone else there
More than half of the votes there
At least a third of the votes there
The most votes across the province
slides.explanation: Coming first in the riding is enough. In the riding of Saint-François the winner had 26.03%, and in 100 of Quebec’s 127 ridings the winner had less than half.

source.label: Élections Québec: results of the general election of 5 October 2026
